name: Seven and one
text: Up at Knappers' Deep, on the lip of Hound Down, the knapper woman keeps a lamp lit at the shaft head every night for the night shift. The roof came down on them eleven winters back. She says they knock. Seven and one, the overman's count. My cousin heard it, lying in the turf with his ear to the old shafts.
variants: Don't lie down on the old shafts round Knappers' Deep. You'll hear them knocking, and once you've heard it you hear it everywhere.

name: Cheap floorstone
text: The man at the Flint Pits is selling floorstone at six marks the sack, and he never dug a sack of it. The Larkbourne Boys go down the ladder at Knappers' Deep and dig it from under Nell Knapper's feet. She won't go to the Wardens. Says the Wardens capped her father in.
variants: If you want black flint cheap, ask at the Flint Pits and don't ask where from. Knappers' Deep, it is. The Boys.

name: Standing on the lip
text: Rookdown won't go up past the mill after dark this summer. The Hum Stone on the lip hums with the Toll now, and the dead come up the cliff out of the Hush to stand by it and listen. They don't do anything. Merrowby's bellwright is camped out there with a cart of hand-bells. He doesn't do anything either.
variants: The old stone on the Brow's lip has started humming. The grey's come up round it on the cliff side. Don't stand there after dark.

name: The cracked bells
text: Two of Merrowby's family bells have cracked since the spring, the Cresswells' and the Ashdowns', in the night, hanging in their trees with nobody near them. Godwin the bellwright says it's the diggers cutting the bronze off the Hum Stone. Godwin also says the Toll is trying to tell us something, so.
variants: You heard about the Cresswells' bell? Cracked in the night. Then the Ashdowns'. Godwin's gone out to the Brow about it.
